hindi: मधुर और हृद्य यानी मन को भाने वाले दे; फिर अम्ल यानी खट्टे और लवण यानी नमकीन, ये दो रस दे।
english: One should give sweet and agreeable (ones); then the two tastes (rasa), sour (amla) and salty (lavaṇa).
notes: The things to be given (the object of dadyāt) are not named for 'madhurahṛdyāni' (neuter plural, 'sweet and agreeable'); the verb is carried to 'amlalavaṇau rasau'. Taste names: madhura sweet, amla sour, lavaṇa salty. GROUPING: units 75-79 appear to form one passage (a graded return to the natural state, closing in 79 with 'prakṛtiṃ gataḥ'); the opening of the passage is not in this unit.

hindi: वैसे ही फिर मधुर और तिक्त यानी कड़वे, उसके बाद कसैले और कटु यानी तीखे।
english: Likewise again the sweet (svādu) and bitter (tikta) ones, then the astringent (kaṣāya) and pungent (kaṭuka) ones.
notes: Elliptical: 'dadyāt' and 'rasau' are carried from unit 75. kaṣāya here is the astringent taste (it stands in a list of tastes), not a decoction. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 75.

hindi: परस्पर विरोधी रसों के और स्निग्ध यानी चिकने तथा रूक्ष यानी रूखे के
english: Of the mutually opposed tastes, and of the unctuous and the dry,
notes: GROUPING: unit 77 is a series of genitives and appears to be one sentence with unit 78 (they depend on 'upayogena' there). 'snigdharūkṣayoḥ' is dual and could be genitive or locative; no noun is stated for 'the unctuous and the dry'. An alternative reading is 'of the tastes, which are opposed to each other, and of the unctuous and the dry'.

hindi: बारी-बारी से यानी अदल-बदल कर प्रयोग करने से क्रम से उसे उसकी प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था तक ले जाए।
english: By using them in alternation, in due order, one should lead him to his natural state (prakṛti).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 77: 'by the use, through alternation, of the mutually opposed tastes and of the unctuous and the dry'. vyatyāsa = interchange, alternation (or reversal of order). prakṛti is read as the person's natural, normal state; the line does not define it. 'taṃ' is the person treated (not named).

hindi: प्रकृति को प्राप्त हुआ, सब कुछ सहने वाला और स्थिर बल वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: One who has reached his natural state (prakṛti) is to be known as all-enduring and of steady strength.
notes: The subject is not named (a masculine singular person). 'sarvasaha' = able to bear everything (lit. all-bearing); the line does not say what he bears.

hindi: इस अन्तर में विशेष रूप से बोलना आदि आठ को छोड़े।
english: In this interval one should give up, especially, the eight (ones) beginning with speaking (bhāṣya).
notes: The eight are not listed in this line. Units 81-93 name causes in turn (loud speaking and, on the printed readings, excessive sitting, riding, walking about, eating while undigested, unsuitable food, day-sleep, sexual intercourse); that these are the eight is not stated. GROUPING: units 80-95 appear to form one passage. bhāṣya = speaking (cf. 'uccair bhāṣya' in 81).

hindi: ऊँचे बोलने से सिर का रोग, तिमिर यानी दृष्टि की धुँधलाहट, और छाती तथा स्वर की पीड़ाएँ
english: From speaking loudly: head disease, timira (dimness of vision), and pains of the chest and voice
notes: Elliptical list: no verb (the sense is a list of ailments arising from loud speaking). timira is the Ayurvedic vision disorder of dimming or darkening of sight (probable; some take it as an early cataract-like state). 'urassvaravyathāḥ' is read as 'pains of the chest and voice'; alternatively 'chest(-pain) and voice-pain'. GROUPING: the list appears to continue in unit 82.

hindi: कल्पित पाठ पर: रक्त का थूकना, मक जो अस्पष्ट है, ज्वर आदि; उस स्थिति में साधन यानी उपचार
english: On a conjectural reading: spitting of blood, 'maka' (unclear), fever and so on; in that case the remedy (sādhana)

text_flags.why: possible: 'maka' is not a word. 'kāsa' (cough) would suit a list of blood-spitting, cough and fever and has the same syllable count, but this is only a guess; the translation does not adopt it

notes: 'maka' is kept as printed and marked unclear; the compound is read as 'rakta-niṣṭhīvana-maka-jvara-ādyāḥ' = 'spitting of blood, maka, fever, and so on'. Elliptical: no verb, the remedies follow in 83-84. GROUPING: continues 81 (list of ailments) and to lead into 83-84 (the remedies).

hindi: कल्पित पाठ पर: अभ्यंग यानी तेल मालिश, स्वेदन यानी पसीना लाना, नस्य यानी नाक में औषधि डालना, और भोजन के बाद स्नेह का सेवन
english: On a conjectural reading: anointing (abhyaṅga, oil massage), sweating (svedana), [nasya, nasal medication] and the use of unctuous substances (sneha) taken after food (adhobhakta)

text_flags.why: possible: 'svedanasya' is not a regular form; 'svedana-nasya' (sweating, nasal medication) fits a remedy list for head and throat ailments after loud speaking, and a syllable 'na' may have dropped; the conjectured 'nasya' is shown in brackets in the English

notes: The printed compound is 'abhyaṅga-svedana-sya-…'; the reading 'nasya' is a conjecture and therefore low confidence. The first three members and 'adhobhakta-sneha-upasevana' are otherwise clear. adhobhakta = taken after food. The compound is read as one list of remedies for the ailments of 81-82. GROUPING: appears to continue 82 'tatra sādhanam' and to lead into 84.

hindi: मौन; वात को हरने वाली विधि; अथवा अपने-अपने अनुसार विकार को जीतने वाला।
english: Silence (mauna); the procedure that removes Vāta; or, as is proper to each, one that conquers the disorder.
notes: Elliptical list without a verb. 'vidhirvātaharaḥ' is taken as one item ('a Vāta-removing procedure'); 'maunaṃ' as a separate item. 'yathāsvam' = each according to its own (case). GROUPING: appears to continue 83 (list of remedies).

words.gloss: unclear; probably 'excessive sitting' (ati-āsyā) and 'riding, travel by vehicle' (yāna)
joint; head; trika (lower back at the sacrum; probable); beginning with; pain

hindi: कल्पित पाठ पर: अत्यधिक बैठने और यान से जाने से जोड़ों, सिर, त्रिक यानी रीढ़ के निचले भाग के त्रिकास्थि क्षेत्र, आदि की पीड़ा
english: On a conjectural reading: from excessive sitting and travelling by vehicle, pain of the joints, head, trika (the lower back at the sacrum) and so on

text_flags.why: possible: the printed word has 'yāna' twice and is not clearly analysable; 'ati-āsyā-yānābhyām' (from excessive sitting and riding) fits the sense, but the printed form scans correctly as it stands (8 syllables), so it may be right and only opaque

notes: Low confidence on the first word: kept unsplit with the conjectural sense only. āsyā = sitting (cf. 'āsyāsukha'). trika is the lower-back region where the spine meets the pelvis (probable; commentators differ on the exact area). 'ruk' = ruj, pain. Orthographic normalisation recorded once for the chunk: printed doubled consonants after r (mūrddha, abhivarddhana, varttim) are written without doubling in `w`.

words.gloss: excessive; first part of 'caṅkramaṇāt' (word broken by a space in print)
foot; shank; thigh; sinking; beginning with

hindi: अत्यधिक चलने-फिरने से पैर, पिंडली और जाँघ का सदन यानी अवसाद आदि
english: From excessive walking about: sinking (sadana, exhaustion) of the feet, shanks, thighs and so on

text_flags.why: word broken by a space in print: 'ati-caṅkramaṇāt' (from excessive walking about); certain
possible: 'sadna' lacks a vowel; 'sadana' (sinking, exhaustion) fits the sense and the metre (16 syllables)

notes: No verb: nominal list. sadana = sinking, exhaustion, debility of the limbs. 'ūru' = thigh, 'jaṅghā' = shank (lower leg). GROUPING: appears to continue the list begun in 85.

hindi: उनके लिए वात को हरने वाला सब कुछ, स्नेह और स्वेद आदि, प्रशस्त है।
english: For these, everything that removes Vāta, beginning with oleation (sneha) and sweating (sveda), is recommended.
notes: 'teṣāṃ' refers back to the ailments of 85-86. sneha = oleation (use of unctuous substances).

hindi: अजीर्ण में भोजन करने से आमविष, छर्दि यानी उलटी, ज्वर आदि
english: From eating while undigested (ajīrṇa-bhojana): āma-viṣa, vomiting (chardi), fever (jvara) and so on
notes: 'ajīrṇabhojana' = eating while the previous meal is undigested. 'āmaviṣa' is read as one term (lit. 'raw poison'); an alternative is two items, 'āma' and 'viṣa' (poison). Elliptical: no verb. GROUPING: unit 89 appears to give the remedy for these.

hindi: उस स्थिति में मात्राशितीय में कही गई, आम को नष्ट करने वाली विधि करनी चाहिए।
english: In that case the procedure that destroys āma, as stated in the Mātrāśitīya, is to be applied.

text_flags.why: possible: the 's' looks like a stray letter; 'vidhiḥ āmahā' (procedure, destroyer of āma) gives sense and the same syllable count

notes: 'mātrāśitīya' is the title of a chapter (on the measure of food; probable); the line itself only names it. The reference is to the text's own earlier chapter and is not checked here. GROUPING: appears to give the remedy for the ailments of 88.

hindi: अहित अन्न से दोष के अनुसार रोग हो सकते हैं, और भेषज यानी औषधियाँ भी।
english: From unwholesome food there may be diseases according to the doṣa, and remedies as well.
notes: Elliptical: 'and remedies' is not further qualified; 'yathādoṣam' probably also governs it (remedies according to the doṣa), but the line does not say so. GROUPING: units 88-90 appear to run on in the same style (cause, then diseases and remedy).

words.gloss: halīmaka (a severe stage of pāṇḍu with a greenish-yellow hue; probable); beginning with

hindi: दिन में सोने से हलीमक यानी पाण्डु रोग की उग्र अवस्था आदि गद पहले कहे गए हैं।
english: From day-sleep, halīmaka (a severe stage of the pale-yellow pāṇḍu condition) and the other diseases (gada) have been declared earlier.

text_flags.why: possible: 'divāsvamāt' is not a word; 'divāsvapnāt' (from day-sleep) is the expected form (OCR pna/ma confusion) and halīmaka is a day-sleep ailment

notes: 'purā' = earlier, formerly: the reference is to an earlier passage of the book (not in this chunk). 'proktā' = proktāḥ with the visarga dropped before the voiced 'd' (regular sandhi). 'gada' = disease.

hindi: कफ से जीते हुओं में धूम यानी धुआँ, रूक्ष यानी रूखा अन्न और लङ्घन यानी उपवास का विधान करे।
english: In those overcome by Kapha one should prescribe smoke (dhūma), dry food and fasting (laṅghana, lightening).
notes: 'kaphajiteṣu' is read as 'in (those) conquered by Kapha'; an alternative is 'in Kapha-conquering (cases)'. dhūma = smoke (no preparation is named in the line). laṅghana = lightening, fasting. GROUPING: appears to follow 91 (day-sleep aggravating Kapha is not stated in this unit).

hindi: व्यवाय यानी मैथुन से, जीवन के भ्रंश यानी पतन से, उसके उन-उन वात-रोगों से
english: From sexual intercourse (vyavāya), from the falling away (bhraṃśa) of life (jīvita), by those various Vāta-ailments (anilāmaya) of his
notes: No verb: a series of causes and an instrumental, probably leading into the symptoms of 94-95. 'jīvitabhraṃśa' (lit. 'falling away of life') is taken literally; its exact sense is uncertain. 'anila' = wind (vāta). GROUPING: units 93-95 appear to form one passage (cause, then symptoms).

words.gloss: is being cut off, torn off

hindi: गुदा मानो कटी जा रही है और चेतना मानो घूम रही है।
english: The anus is, as it were, being torn off, and consciousness, as it were, whirls.

text_flags.why: possible: 'avalupyate iva' with the usual change of final e before a vowel gives 'avalupyata iva'; the print joins the two words

notes: GROUPING: units 94-95 appear to continue 93 as a list of symptoms. 'avalupyate' = is cut off, torn away (the sensation of the anus being torn); 'bhramati iva cetanā' = consciousness seems to reel.

hindi: मेढ्र यानी लिंग धुआँ छोड़ता है; मन मानो अन्धकार में प्रवेश करेगा।
english: The penis smokes (emits smoke); the mind will enter, as it were, into darkness.
notes: 'dhūmāyati' is a denominative from dhūma ('smoke') and is translated literally; whether a sensation of heat or smoke is meant is not stated. 'iva' attaches to tamasi: 'as if into darkness'. GROUPING: appears to continue 94.

words.gloss: jīvanī (disputed: the jīvanīya group of life-promoting drugs, or jīvantī, Leptadenia reticulata); filled, laden; milk; ghee

hindi: जीवनी यानी सम्भवतः जीवनीय गण से भरे हुए दूध और घी का प्रयोग
english: The use of milk and ghee filled with jīvanī (probably the jīvanīya group of drugs)

text_flags.why: possible: 'jīvanī' may be 'jīvanīya' (cf. 'sajīvanīyaḥ' in 108; the printed line has 15 syllables where 16 are expected) and 'bhṛta' (filled, laden) may be 'śṛta' (cooked, boiled); both are guesses, and the printed words are translated as they stand

notes: bhṛta literally 'borne, filled'; the printed sense is kept. jīvanī is taken as the jīvanīya group (standard group of ten life-promoting drugs, see 108) but alternatively jīvantī (disputed). Nominal: no verb. GROUPING: appears to run on into 97 ('there: nourishing food, virilising bastis').

hindi: उस स्थिति में बृंहण यानी शरीर को पुष्ट करने वाला आहार, और वे वृष्य यानी शुक्र बढ़ाने वाली बस्तियाँ यानी एनीमा।
english: In that case, food that is bulking (bṛṃhaṇa), and those bastis (enemas) that are virilising (vṛṣya).
notes: Nominal: no verb. vṛṣya = promoting sexual vigour and semen. GROUPING: appears to continue 96.

words.gloss: urge; holding back; upward; wind-humour (vāta); state of

hindi: पहले कहे गए जो सदा आतुर यानी पीड़ित, वेगों के रोकने और ऊर्ध्व वात के कारण
english: Those who, as stated earlier, are always ailing because of holding back of urges and upward Vāta
notes: 'vegarodhordhvavātatvāt' is read as a dvandva 'holding back of urges and the state of upward wind'; the compound could also be read as 'the state of having upward wind from holding back urges'. 'prāk-uktāḥ' refers to an earlier passage not in this chunk. GROUPING: appears to form one sentence with 99-100 ('ye ... teṣām').

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, adj., m. loc. sg. (so read)

hindi: उनमें रुकी हुई, पूरे शरीर को सन्ताप देने वाली वायु में,
english: In them, when the wind (pavana) is obstructed and afflicting the whole body,

text_flags.why: possible: read as the locative 'sarvadehopatāpini' agreeing with 'pavane' (a locative absolute); the printed long ī would be a feminine nominative, which has nothing to agree with here

notes: pavana (wind) = Vāta. An alternative is the feminine nominative 'upatāpinī' qualifying an unstated feminine noun (a pain or the phalavartti of 100); the locative reading is taken. GROUPING: appears to continue from 98 ('ye … teṣām') and to be completed by the verb 'dadyāt' in 100.

hindi: पहले फलवर्ति यानी औषधि की बत्ती दे, फिर बल लाने वाली बस्ति यानी एनीमा दे।
english: One should first give a phalavartti (suppository), then a basti (enema) that brings strength.

text_flags.why: possible: the anusvāra of the object 'phalavarttiṃ' seems to have dropped before 'purā'

notes: phalavartti (lit. 'fruit-wick') = a medicated suppository (standard term). purā here = first, before. Spelling 'vartti' is written 'varti' in `w` (normalisation noted in 85). GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence of 98-99.

words.gloss: nikumbha (disputed: dantī, wild croton, Baliospermum montanum); kumbha (unidentified); agni (probable: citraka, leadwort, Plumbago zeylanica); urubūka (castor, Ricinus communis; standard); dhāvanī (disputed: pṛśniparṇī, Uraria picta)

hindi: निकुम्भ यानी सम्भवतः जंगली जमालगोटा, कुम्भ, अग्नि यानी सम्भवतः चित्रक, उरुबूक यानी अरंडी, धावनी यानी पृश्निपर्णी यानी पिठवन, पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूर्णा, दारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु, और महत् पञ्चक
english: Nikumbha (probably wild croton), kumbha (unidentified), agni (probably leadwort), urubūka (castor), dhāvanī (disputed, perhaps pṛśniparṇī), punarnava (spreading hogweed), dāru (probably deodar) and the great group of five (mahat pañcaka)
notes: Ingredient list: no verb in 101-102; the use is not stated until 103, where 'nirūhita' suggests a nirūha (decoction enema) formula (the line itself states no verb). Identifications: nikumbha disputed (often dantī); kumbha unidentified; agni probable citraka (a common synonym; 104 names citraka separately); urubūka standard (castor); dhāvanī disputed (a recorded synonym of pṛśniparṇī); punarnava standard; dāru probable devadāru; 'mahat pañcaka' unidentified (the text only says 'the great group of five'; possibly the five great roots, disputed, not applied). GROUPING: ingredient list continued in 102 and used in 103.

hindi: और फल, सब मूत्र में उबाला हुआ; घी तैल सहित; पाँच लवण।
english: And the fruit, all boiled together in urine; ghee with oil; five salts.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kathita' means 'said'; 'boiled in urine' calls for 'kvathita' (OCR ka/kva)
possible: 'samastu' does not fit; 'samastam' (all together) agrees with 'kathitam' (OCR ṃ/u confusion)

notes: The fruit is not named (phala only), and the kind of urine is not stated. 'pañca lavaṇāni' = five salts: the usual group is rock salt, black salt, viḍa salt, sea salt and efflorescent salt (probable), but the line does not list them. Elliptical: no verb. GROUPING: appears to continue 101 and to be used in 103.

words.gram: ppp. caus. nir-√ūh, m. acc. sg. (so read)

hindi: जिसे निरूह बस्ति दी जा चुकी हो उसे धन्व-रस यानी सम्भवतः सूखे देश के पशुओं के मांसरस से भोजन कराए, फिर निकुम्भ के तैल से अनुवासन यानी तैल-बस्ति करे।
english: Him who has been given nirūha (decoction enema) one should feed with dhanva-rasa (probably the meat broth of dry-land animals), then give anuvāsana (oil enema) with nikumbha oil.

text_flags.why: possible: the object needs the accusative ending; the final anusvāra seems to have dropped before 'dhanva-')

notes: dhanva-rasa: dhanva = arid country; the usual sense of the term is the juice of the meat of dry-land animals (probable), but the line only says 'dhanva-rasa'. nikumbha oil: made from nikumbha (see 101; not stated how). The verb 'anuvāsayet' governs the same unnamed person. GROUPING: appears to complete the formula of 101-102 (the line does not say the formula is for nirūha).

words.gloss: with; rāsnā (disputed: Pluchea lanceolata or Alpinia galanga)
two; five; root (the ten roots, daśamūla; standard group)
from kṛtamālaka (Indian laburnum, Cassia fistula; standard)

hindi: बला यानी खरेटी रास्ना सहित; चित्रक यानी चीता से फल और मूल; द्विपञ्चमूल यानी दशमूल; कृतमालक यानी अमलतास से फल
english: Balā (country mallow) with rāsnā (identity disputed); the fruit and root from citraka (leadwort); the ten roots (dvipañcamūla); the fruit from kṛtamālaka (Indian laburnum)

text_flags.why: possible: 'dvipañcamūlam' (the ten roots) with the 'v' of 'dvi' dropped (OCR dv/dd confusion); the printed doubled 'dd' fits this

notes: Low confidence on the grouping: 'phalamūlacitrakāt' is read as 'the fruit and root from citraka' (ablative of source, as in 'kṛtamālakāt phalam'); an alternative is three separate items (fruit, root, and citraka). The accusative objects are not governed by a verb until 'pacet' in 105. 'baḻāṃ' is printed with ḻ (ळ) for l; written balām in `w`. rāsnā disputed; citraka and kṛtamālaka standard. GROUPING: appears to be one sentence with 105 (ingredients, then 'pacet').

words.gloss: with; musta (nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; standard); pāṭhā (velvet-leaf, Cissampelos pareira; probable); indrayava (seed of kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica; standard)

hindi: यव और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी को जल में पकाए; रस, मुस्त यानी नागरमोथा, पाठा और इन्द्रयव यानी इन्द्रजौ के साथ, कल्क से युक्त।
english: Barley (yava) and horse gram (kulattha): one should boil in water; the rasa (extract) has a paste (kalka) with musta (nut-grass), pāṭhā and indrayava (kurchi seed).
notes: The objects of 'pacet' include the items of 104 (not stated in this unit). 'rasa' here is the extract resulting from boiling; the text does not say 'decoction'. The paste is taken as made from or with musta, pāṭhā and indrayava. GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence begun in 104. Units 101-106 appear to give two formulas (101-103 and 104-106); the line does not say so.

words.gloss: first part of guḍa (word broken by a space in print)

hindi: तैल और घी, गुड़ और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक के साथ, सदा आतुरों के लिए हितकर, बल, पुष्टि और वर्ण देने वाला।
english: With oil and ghee, jaggery and rock salt (saindhava), it is beneficial to those who are always ailing, giving strength, nourishment and complexion.

text_flags.why: word 'guḍa' broken by a space in print; certain

notes: The subject (the rasa of 105) is not restated in this unit. 'sadā āturāṇām' is read as 'of the always-ailing' (cf. 98); alternatively 'always beneficial to the ailing'. 'bala-puṣṭi-varṇa-da' = giving strength, nourishment and (good) complexion. The printed token ''turāṇāṃ' has the avagraha pair for 'ā' (hiatus after sadā). GROUPING: appears to complete the formula of 104-105.

words.gloss: to be given as anuvāsana (oil enema)
with madhuka (probably liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; probable)
with śatāhvayā (probable: śatāhvā, dill, Anethum sowa)

hindi: वैसे ही अनुवासन के योग्य, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी से, कोमल बिल्व यानी बेल से, अथवा शताह्वया यानी सम्भवतः सोआ से तैयार किया हुआ।
english: Likewise, what is to be given as anuvāsana (oil enema), prepared with madhuka (probably liquorice), with young bilva (bael), or with śatāhvayā (probably dill).

text_flags.why: possible: the letters 'vh' look transposed for 'hv': śatāhvayā

notes: 'anuvāsya' (neuter) is a substance fit for anuvāsana; the substance itself (oil, ghee) is not named. 'bālena bilvena' is read as 'with young bilva'; an alternative is two drugs, bāla (a fragrant root, hrīvera, disputed) and bilva. śatāhvayā: probable dill; it could also be śatāvarī (asparagus), disputed. madhuka: probable liquorice (earlier in this book likewise); it could be the mahua tree. GROUPING: appears to follow 106 and to be completed by 108.

words.gloss: with; jīvanīya (the group of ten life-promoting drugs; standard)

hindi: शिशु के लिए अनुवासन यानी तैल-बस्ति में जीवनीय गण के साथ रस हितकर है, और निरूहण यानी निरूह बस्ति में बिना नमक का।
english: But for a child the rasa with jīvanīya (drugs) is beneficial in anuvāsana (oil enema), and in nirūhaṇa (decoction enema) the one without salt.
notes: jīvanīya group (standard, from the Caraka list; not checked against this book): jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka. 'śiśoḥ hitaḥ' governs both halves; 'hitaḥ' is carried to 'alavaṇaḥ'. GROUPING: appears to follow 107.

hindi: और निरूह बस्ति से बढ़कर दूसरा कोई शीघ्र अंगों का बल बढ़ाने वाला नहीं; शिशु और वृद्ध से भिन्नों के लिए हितकर।
english: And there is no other quick increaser of the strength of the limbs than nirūha basti (decoction enema); beneficial to those who are neither child nor aged.
notes: 'nirūhabasteḥ' is read as an ablative of comparison ('than nirūha-basti'); a genitive reading is also possible. 'aśiśuvṛddhayoḥ' is read as 'of the not-child and not-aged'; an alternative is 'of the non-child and the aged'. The verb is not stated ('is'). GROUPING: appears to close the chapter's teaching before the colophon 110.

words.gloss: Sneha-vyāpat-siddhi (the cure of the complications of oleation)

hindi: इस प्रकार स्नेहव्यापत्सिद्धि नामक सप्तम अध्याय।
english: Thus the seventh chapter, named Sneha-vyāpat-siddhi (the cure of the complications of oleation).
notes: GROUPING: this appears to be the chapter colophon, not a verse; it is typed as a verse in the input. The opening || is a printed mark. The title is read as sneha-vyāpat-siddhi 'cure (siddhi) of the complications (vyāpad) of oleation (sneha)'. The closing 'iti' belongs to the colophon formula.
